text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Bomb explosion kills eight and wounds 37 at an Algiers market. Two home-made bombs have killed seven and wounded 86 inside passenger buses in Algiers the day before.
- End of campaigning for Thursday's parliamentary election.
- Army troops and security forces cast ballots.
- Trade union UGTA urges workers to vote for anti-Islamist candidates.

- Candidates made last pitches for voters at the end of poll campaigning on Monday. Rally for Culture and Democracy leader Said Saadi urges anti-Islamists to unite ranks. Left-wing Workers Party spokeswoman Louisa Hanoune wants a televised debate with Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia on election issues. All three are candidates in Algiers.
- Bomb kills 11 people at market in Algiers. The government calls on residents to report suspected booby-trapped cars and parcels.
- Security forces kill 11 terrorists in Algiers.
- The authorities shut down schools in Algiers because of bombing fears in the city.
